I ask what's going on and he says like "sorry, do you think you can help me clean? Keep falling down" He was speaking weird like speaking was annoying him. As you mentioned, this annual experience can "shift what feels important." It's likely that, over time, people who observe Ramadan may develop a greater appreciation for the values and principles that are emphasized during this month, such as kindness, generosity, and self-reflection. These values can, in turn, influence their priorities and decisions throughout the year, even after the month of Ramadan has ended. It's a beautiful example of how a collective, spiritual practice can shape individual values and contribute to personal growth, community cohesion, and a deeper sense of purpose.
